title: In 1752, Britain went to bed on 2 September and woke on the 14th
body: To switch from the Julian to the Gregorian calendar, which Catholic Europe had used since 1582, Britain and its colonies dropped eleven days: Wednesday 2 September 1752 was followed by Thursday 14 September. Rent and contract dates were shifted so nobody gained or lost, which is why the UK tax year still ends on 5 April. Tales of mobs demanding ‘give us our eleven days’ are very likely a myth.
